subject: EuroHealth RFP: elective data residency & hosting clarification
messages:
From: Sofie Lemaire <sofie.lemaire@eurohealthsystems.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
Cc: procurement@eurohealthsystems.com
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: RFP Q: elective residency / cross-region backups

Hi Laura,

Thanks for taking time to review EuroHealth's RFP. A couple of clarifications from procurement and IT before we proceed to the commercial redlines:

1) Our RFP asks for EU-only data residency for patient PII and system logs unless explicit written consent is provided by the controller. Can Redwood guarantee that production data and backups remain within EU regions (Frankfurt/Paris/Amsterdam) by default?

2) We understand some vendors use multi-region replication for durability. If Redwood uses cross-region replication for DR, can you provide the list of regions used and whether customers can opt-out?

3) Our security team is also asking whether edge inference in Frankfurt can be configured to prevent any inference traffic from leaving the EU region (including control-plane metadata).

Attached: EH_RFP_Q1.pdf (excerpt). Please confirm what statements we can include in the procurement pack and whether you can provide a short formal residency statement for signature.

Would love a short call early next week if needed.

Best,
Sofie
Sofie Lemaire
Senior Sourcing Manager, EuroHealth Systems

From: laura.bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 12:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: RFP Q: elective residency / cross-region backups

Hi Sofie — thanks, and good questions. Answering at a high level here and we'll follow with a short formal statement for procurement: 

- EU-default residency: Redwood Private and Hosted enterprise tenants can be configured with an EU-only data residency policy. When you select an EU tenancy, all customer-controlled data (user content, logs tagged to the tenant, and model inputs/outputs) are stored in customer-designated EU regions (we commonly use eu-central-1/frankfurt and eu-west-1/ireland).

- Cross-region replication & DR: By default we do not replicate production data outside the tenant's designated region unless configured for multi-region DR. For Dedicated/Private customers we offer an opt-in cross-region DR runbook; locations used are customer-configurable and require explicit contract language.

- Edge inference control-plane metadata: We support a private control plane for our Private product. If you run the Private control plane in your VPC (or our EU-managed Private offering), control-plane metadata remains in-region and can be integrated with your KMS/HSM — no metadata leaves the EU.

Attachments we're preparing: a technical residency matrix (Marissa will add deployment specifics) and a one-page signed residency commitment for procurement.

Proposed next step: 30-minute call Thu (15 Jul) or Mon (19 Jul) to walk through any redline language. Which works for you?

Thanks — Laura
Laura Bennett

Subject: Re: RFP Q: elective residency / cross-region backups

Hi Sofie — following up with the technical matrix you asked for. See attached residency_matrix_v1.xlsx which maps data classes and default storage/replication behavior. Key snippets below: 

- Data classification mapping: PII, PHI, logs, model telemetry, aggregated metrics. PII/PHI are tagged as tenant-sensitive and stored in tenant-designated EU regions by default.
- Backups: Automated daily snapshots are stored in the tenant region. For Dedicated/Private customers, we offer optional cross-region backups for DR; this is opt-in and gated behind contract language.
- Disaster recovery test cadence: quarterly DR failover tests available as an add-on.
- KMS/HSM: Customer-managed keys supported for Private — keys remain in the customer's KMS region.

We also included an example clause you can copy into procurement: "Provider shall store and process Customer Data within the EU as designated by Customer and shall not replicate Customer Data outside of the EU without Customer's prior written consent, except as required by law." Happy to make that more specific to the contract template you prefer.

On the control-plane: if you choose our Private control plane deployed in your VPC, orchestration and metadata remain in-region. For Hosted+Dedicated customers we offer a shared control plane with strict EU-only routing for tenants whose account is EU-resident; we will provide the technical logs and traceability during SOC2/audit review.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Architect, Inference Platform

Hi Laura/Marissa — this is helpful, thank you. A couple of follow-ups from procurement and security: 

1) Procurement wants a short, signed statement (one page) we can attach to the contract that says: "Provider will store Customer Data in the EU and will not transfer backups outside the EU without prior written consent." Can Redwood provide that on company letterhead?

2) Security asks for confirmation that when using Hosted/Dedicated (not Private), logs that include request metadata will not be shipped to US-based analytics services by default. We need explicit assurance or a list of analytics endpoints.

3) Regarding edge inference in Frankfurt: our clinical apps will require deterministic routing — can you confirm the ability to pin inference workloads to a Frankfurt-only pool and have health checks/fallback stay within EU regions?

If you can send the one-page statement and suggested contract language by Wed EOD we can slot it into our procurement packet.

Best — Sofie

Hi Sofie — attaching a formal residency commitment and proposed contract language. See attached: Residency_Commitment_statement.docx. Key points summarized below for procurement and security: 

1) Residency commitment (company letterhead): "Redwood Inference will store and process Customer Data in Customer-designated EU regions and will not transfer Customer Data or backups outside the EU without Customer's prior written consent. For Dedicated/Private customers, cross-region DR is strictly opt-in and requires documented approval."

2) Hosted/Dedicated telemetry: default analytics endpoints and telemetry collectors used by Hosted are hosted in the EU for EU-resident tenants. We will provide a full list of endpoints and CSV export for Security during the audit package handoff. If Customer requires, we can route telemetry to Customer-managed endpoints or disable certain analytics at provisioning.

3) Frankfurt-only inference pool: We can pin inference workloads to a Frankfurt-only pool and configure fallback policies that restrict failover to EU regions only. The fallback playbook includes health checks and explicit canary windows; failover to non-EU regions will not occur without explicit written authorization.

Next steps: 1) I can provide a signed PDF of the residency statement on Redwood letterhead by EOD Thu (22 Jul). 2) If procurement approves the sample clause below, we'll prepare the DocuSign envelope for signature. 

Suggested clause for SOW/SLA: "Provider shall ensure all Customer Data (as defined in the Agreement) is stored and processed within Customer-designated EU regions and will not replicate or transfer such data outside the EU except with Customer's prior written consent. Provider agrees to provide endpoint and telemetry mappings and cooperate with Customer's audit requests related to residency."

Please confirm if this wording is acceptable and we will send the signed statement and DocuSign link.

Regards,
